summary: The root همر (hmr) primarily means to pour out, like water or tears. It can also refer to drawing out all the milk from an udder, giving generously from one's property, or speaking voluminously.
lane: 1 هَمَرَهُ ذ , (S, A, K,) aor. هَمُرَ (S, K) and هَمِرَ , (K,) inf. n. هَمْرٌ , (S,) He, or it, poured it; out or forth; (S, A, K;) namely, water, (S, TA,) and tears, and rain, and the like. (TA.) -b2- هَمَرَ مَا فِى الضَّرْعِ He drew forth all the milk that was in the udder. (S, K.) -b3- هَمَرَ لَهُ مِنْ مَالِهِ (assumed tropical:) He gave to him of his property. (S, K.) -b4- هَمَرَ الكَلَامَ , (K,) or فى كَلَامِهِ , (A,) aor. هَمُرَ , inf. n. هَمْرٌ : (TA;) and بِالكَلَامِ ; (S;) (tropical:) He talked much. (K.) -A2- هَمَرَ , intrans.: see 7. in two places.
